where κρείσσονες [the stronger ones] are opposed to Oceanus, a god of lower rank. Hesychius records that κρείττονες [the stronger ones] was used of the gods by Aeschylus in the Aetnaeae (fr. 7).

played on the lyre, sung
an adjective derived from κρέκειν [to strike the lyre], which is said of playing the cithara: hence sung

Thus Hermann for ὁμοῦ κρεκτὸν γοήτων [together a sung (nomos) of wailers] (γοητῶν [of wailers] M by a later hand) νόμον μεθήσομεν πόλει [we shall release a nomos for the city]. The word is not found elsewhere, except that Hesychius noted θρεκτοῖσι νόμοις [with struck nomoi] instead of τροχαίοις [trochaic], Sophocles in Odysseus Mad; but some read κρεκτοῖς [struck], and rightly so, if any weight is to be given to the similarity of the Aeschylean passage.
And together we shall set a sung nomos of wailers for the city.
